issues.legal_issue: A delayed statutory appeal may be admitted only when the applicant establishes a sufficient cause that prevented timely filing.
material_facts: The appeals were filed about five and a half years after the reference court’s award.
The only explanation offered for the delay was that one appellant had been ill.
The explanation was not found sufficient to account for the delay.
issues.conclusion: The delay was not condoned, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 permits condonation only upon sufficient cause. Sufficient cause requires an adequate explanation showing that the applicant was prevented from acting in time; negligence, inaction or lack of bona fides defeats the application. The court must exercise its discretion judicially, while giving the expression a liberal interpretation only where those defects cannot be imputed. The Court relied on Manindra Land and Building Corporation Ltd. v. Bhootnath Banerjee, Lala Matadin v. A. Narayanan, Parimal v. Veena, Maniben Devraj Shah v. Municipal Corporation of Brihan Mumbai, Madanlal v. Shyamlal, and Ram Nath Sao v. Gobardhan Sao.

rule.if: delayed_statutory_appeal and substantial_delay and only_illness_explanation and no_satisfactory_cause

predicates.delayed_statutory_appeal: The applicant filed a statutory appeal after the prescribed filing period.
predicates.substantial_delay: The appeal was filed substantially later than the prescribed period.
predicates.only_illness_explanation: The applicant relied only on an appellant’s illness to explain the late filing.
predicates.no_satisfactory_cause: The applicant did not satisfactorily explain what prevented timely filing.

issues.definition: When a statutory appeal is substantially late and the only explanation is illness without a satisfactory account of the delay, the delay is not condoned.

issues.legal_issue: Equal treatment does not entitle a litigant to relief merely because similar litigants previously received relief through erroneous orders.
material_facts: The appellants relied on other similar matters in which delay had been condoned on the condition that interest would not be paid for the period of delay.
The Court considered those orders erroneous because they had been made without addressing the requirement of sufficient cause.
issues.conclusion: The earlier orders did not entitle the appellants to the same relief; an erroneous or illegal order cannot be repeated on grounds of equality.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 of the Constitution does not provide negative equality or require the repetition of an illegality. The Court relied on Chandigarh Administration v. Jagjit Singh, M/s. Anand Button Ltd. v. State of Haryana, K.K. Bhalla v. State of M.P., and Fuljit Kaur v. State of Punjab.

predicates.delayed_statutory_appeal: The matter concerns a statutory appeal filed after the prescribed period.
predicates.equal_treatment_claim: The applicant seeks the same relief as other litigants on the ground of equal treatment.
predicates.prior_similar_relief_granted_erroneously: Other litigants received similar relief through orders that failed to apply the governing legal requirements.

issues.definition: A litigant appealing after the prescribed period cannot obtain equal relief solely because similar litigants previously received it through erroneous orders.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot condone delay without sufficient cause by imposing a condition that limits the relief otherwise available to the applicant.
material_facts: In similar matters, delay had been condoned on the condition that claimants would not receive interest for the period of delay.
The Court held that such orders were made without considering sufficient cause and could not be approved.
issues.conclusion: A court cannot justify condoning delay without sufficient cause by imposing a condition, including a restriction on interest for the period of delay.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 requires the court to determine whether sufficient cause prevented timely filing. Where there is no sufficient cause, conditional condonation still violates the statutory requirements. The Court also applied the principle that limitation must be enforced as prescribed and cannot be extended on equitable grounds.

predicates.delayed_statutory_appeal: The matter concerns an appeal filed after the prescribed period.
predicates.no_sufficient_cause: The applicant has not established an adequate reason that prevented timely filing.
predicates.conditional_condonation_proposed: The court proposes to admit the late appeal subject to a condition limiting the applicant’s relief.

issues.definition: When an appeal is late, sufficient cause is absent, and admission is proposed subject to a condition, the delay cannot be condoned by imposing that condition.
